claims.text: A conventional automotive exhaust catalyst can consist of Pt nanoparticles supported on gamma-Al2O3.
The proposed intervention combines cerium doping of the support with ALD deposition of Pt.
ALD will produce atomically dispersed Pt on the Ce-doped support.
Cerium incorporation increases the oxygen-storage capacity of the support.
Cerium incorporation promotes strong metal-support interactions.
Strong metal-support interactions stabilize isolated Pt atoms.
Stabilization of isolated Pt atoms prevents or minimizes Pt sintering and agglomeration at high temperature.
Atomically dispersed Pt provides more active surface area per unit mass of precious metal than Pt nanoparticles.
Cerium enhances the redox functionality of the support.
Enhanced support redox functionality facilitates rapid oxygen transfer.
Suppression of Pt agglomeration leads to sustained catalytic performance and improved resistance to thermal sintering.
The Ce-doped, atomically dispersed Pt catalyst will provide higher conversion efficiencies for NOx, CO, and hydrocarbons than Pt nanoparticles on undoped gamma-Al2O3.
The Ce-doped, atomically dispersed Pt catalyst will retain more catalytic activity after prolonged high-temperature cycling than the baseline catalyst.
The Ce-doped, atomically dispersed Pt catalyst will require a lower overall Pt loading to achieve high or comparable activity.
The predicted improvements are expected during moderate lean-rich redox cycling between 500 and 800 degrees Celsius.
Performance outside 500 to 800 degrees Celsius or under extremely fuel-rich conditions is uncertain.
The magnitude of improvement and the optimal Ce content and ALD conditions require empirical optimization.
